candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a two-part composite: Poncet's Disease (the reactive, non-infectious polyarthritis driven by TB hypersensitivity, evidenced by sterile joint fluid, large-joint involvement, and no direct joint infection) plus tuberculous lymphadenitis (confirmed by AFB-positive cervical node biopsy with caseating granulomas). C001 correctly identifies tuberculosis and its granulomatous/AFB features but does not specify Poncet's Disease as the arthritis mechanism nor name tuberculous lymphadenitis as a discrete component. It is therefore a parent-level label missing the required specificity of both composite elements.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Names the parent disease (tuberculosis) and histopathological findings but omits both required composite components: Poncet's Disease (reactive tuberculous polyarthritis) and tuberculous lymphadenitis as distinct named entities

case_quality_flags: Paradoxically low ESR (6 mm/h) despite markedly elevated CRP (131 mg/L) is unusual but does not alter the diagnostic conclusion
Poncet's Disease is a rare reactive arthritis; its distinction from direct septic TB arthritis rests on sterile cultures and normal joint radiographs, both present here
